DATABASE courtside_nba: NBA 2025-26 regular season: 1,230 games from 2025-10-21 to 2026-04-12, every five-man lineup rebuilt from play-by-play with an estimate of how much of each lineup's rating is real, per-player box scores, player impact (RAPM), play-type efficiency, and 2026-27 contracts. Descriptive, not predictive: it holds no forecasts.

SCOPE
- stats: 2025-26 regular season only. No playoffs, no other seasons.
- contracts: 2026-27 salaries (NEXT season), not the salaries paid in 2025-26.
- refuse when: The question needs another season, the playoffs, a prediction or betting advice, or data this database does not hold (injuries, news, draft, shot locations, tracking data).

RULES (follow every one)
1. [rank_lineups_honestly] Never rank lineups by raw net_rating. Lineups with a handful of possessions have ratings like +600. Rank by `shrunk` (the noise-corrected estimate) or filter to poss >= 100 and say so. Always report poss with any lineup rating.
2. [distinguishable_is_rare] `distinguishable = 1` means the 95% interval (lo95 to hi95) excludes the LEAGUE-AVERAGE lineup rating (mu = -0.68), not zero. Only 4 of 17,733 lineups qualify. When asked for the "best" lineup, say how few are statistically separable from average instead of presenting a clean winner.
3. [games_played_means_minutes_not_null] player_game_stats has one row per rostered player per game, including players who did not play. minutes IS NULL means did not play (5,528 rows, all with zero stats). For per-game averages or games played, filter minutes IS NOT NULL (3 more rows have minutes = 0).
4. [contracts_are_next_season] contracts hold 2026-27 salaries while all performance data is 2025-26. When combining them, say so. 6 traded players have two contract rows (one per team) with the SAME salary, so any total, average or count over players that is not split by team (league-wide, by option, by salary band) must count each player once: aggregate over (SELECT DISTINCT player_id, salary, ... FROM contracts). A team's payroll counts every row on that team.
5. [lineup_keys] Join lineup_stats, lineup_bootstrap on lineup_uid only (it contains the season and team). lineup_bootstrap lacks 32 lineups, so use LEFT JOIN from lineup_stats.
6. [find_player_in_lineup] lineup_stats.lineup is player ids joined by '-'. To test membership use ('-' || lineup || '-') LIKE ('%-' || <player_id> || '-%'). A bare LIKE '%<id>%' also matches longer ids. lineup_stats.players holds FAMILY NAMES only, comma-separated.
7. [names_and_ids] Resolve a person to player_id first, then filter by id. players has first_name and family_name (with diacritics, e.g. Jokić, Šarić). Full name = first_name || ' ' || family_name. Teams: team columns named `team` and *_abbr hold 3-letter abbreviations (BOS); *_team_id columns hold ids; join teams to translate.
8. [units] Ratings are points per 100 possessions. poss is a real number because possessions are split half-and-half between the two sides. Percentages in *_pct columns are fractions 0-1. Salaries are whole US dollars.
9. [players_traded] A player's team is a fact about a game, not the player (players has no team_id). Use player_game_stats.team_id for who a player played for. player_season.teams is text like 'WAS → DAL' for a traded player.
10. [games_results] games has home and away points, no winner column and no ties. Home win = home_pts > away_pts. Each team plays 82 games. game_date is ISO text (YYYY-MM-DD).
11. [always_bound_results] Add LIMIT to any query that lists rows, and prefer aggregating in SQL.

METRICS
- off_rating: pts_for / poss_for * 100: points scored per 100 possessions.
- def_rating: pts_against / poss_against * 100: points allowed per 100 possessions (lower is better).
- net_rating: off_rating - def_rating, per 100 possessions. Observed, noisy, garbage time excluded.
- poss: Possessions the lineup played, (poss_for + poss_against) / 2. The sample size.
- shrunk: Empirical-Bayes estimate of the lineup's true net rating: the observed rating pulled toward the league mean (-0.68) in proportion to how little was observed. Use this to rank lineups.
- post_sd: Posterior standard deviation of shrunk. lo95/hi95 = shrunk -/+ 1.96 * post_sd.
- weight: Share of the observed rating that survives shrinkage, 0-1; rises with possessions.
- distinguishable: 1 if the 95% interval excludes the league-average lineup rating, i.e. lo95 > mu or hi95 < mu where mu = noise_model.mu (-0.68); else 0. Two of the four flagged lineups have lo95 slightly below 0, so this is NOT the same as "excludes zero".
- net_rating_luck: net_rating after resetting OPPONENT three-point and free-throw conversion to league rates (36.1% and 78.4%); attempts are unchanged. A luck-adjusted view of the same lineup.
- rapm: Regularised adjusted plus-minus: a player's estimated impact in points per 100 possessions after adjusting for teammates and opponents. o_rapm + d_rapm = rapm. Pooled across all loaded seasons (here only 2025-26). Noisy below a few thousand possessions; check poss.
- ppp: Points per possession in a play type. For defence this is points ALLOWED per possession, so lower is better.

- games [one row per game]: Final scores of the 1,230 regular-season games.

- player_season [one row per player (577)]: Season totals of on-court possessions and net margin per player.

- coverage_team [one row per team (30)]: Data quality per team.
- contracts [one row per player per team (414 rows, 408 players)]: 2026-27 player contracts.
- cap_rules [one row per season]: Salary cap thresholds for 2025-26 and 2026-27 (two rows).
- player_positions [one row per player (582)]: Listed position per player.
- play_types [one row per play type]: Lookup of the 11 play types.

- provenance [one row per table]: Where each table in this database was copied from. Not useful for basketball questions.

args.query:
SELECT 
    p.first_name || ' ' || p.family_name AS player_name,
    SUM(pgs.points) AS total_points
FROM player_game_stats pgs
JOIN players p ON pgs.player_id = p.player_id
WHERE pgs.minutes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY pgs.player_id
ORDER BY total_points DESC
LIMIT 5;

args.query:
WITH team_wins AS (
  SELECT team_id, SUM(wins) AS wins FROM (
    SELECT home_team_id AS team_id, CASE WHEN home_pts > away_pts THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wins FROM games
    UNION ALL
    SELECT away_team_id AS team_id, CASE WHEN away_pts > home_pts THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wins FROM games
  ) GROUP BY team_id
),
top_team AS (
  SELECT team_id FROM team_wins ORDER BY wins DESC LIMIT 1
)
SELECT t.city || ' ' || t.name AS team_name, MAX(c.salary) AS max_salary, tw.wins
FROM contracts c
JOIN top_team tt ON c.team_id = tt.team_id
JOIN team_wins tw ON tw.team_id = tt.team_id
JOIN teams t ON t.team_id = tt.team_id
GROUP BY c.team_id;

DATABASE courtside_nba: NBA 2025-26 regular season: 1,230 games from 2025-10-21 to 2026-04-12, every five-man lineup rebuilt from play-by-play with an estimate of how much of each lineup's rating is real, per-player box scores, player impact (RAPM), play-type efficiency, and 2026-27 contracts. Descriptive, not predictive: it holds no forecasts.

SCOPE
- stats: 2025-26 regular season only. No playoffs, no other seasons.
- contracts: 2026-27 salaries (NEXT season), not the salaries paid in 2025-26.
- refuse when: The question needs another season, the playoffs, a prediction or betting advice, or data this database does not hold (injuries, news, draft, shot locations, tracking data).

RULES (follow every one)
1. [rank_lineups_honestly] Never rank lineups by raw net_rating. Lineups with a handful of possessions have ratings like +600. Rank by `shrunk` (the noise-corrected estimate) or filter to poss >= 100 and say so. Always report poss with any lineup rating.
2. [distinguishable_is_rare] `distinguishable = 1` means the 95% interval (lo95 to hi95) excludes the LEAGUE-AVERAGE lineup rating (mu = -0.68), not zero. Only 4 of 17,733 lineups qualify. When asked for the "best" lineup, say how few are statistically separable from average instead of presenting a clean winner.
3. [games_played_means_minutes_not_null] player_game_stats has one row per rostered player per game, including players who did not play. minutes IS NULL means did not play (5,528 rows, all with zero stats). For per-game averages or games played, filter minutes IS NOT NULL (3 more rows have minutes = 0).
4. [contracts_are_next_season] contracts hold 2026-27 salaries while all performance data is 2025-26. When combining them, say so. 6 traded players have two contract rows (one per team) with the SAME salary, so any total, average or count over players that is not split by team (league-wide, by option, by salary band) must count each player once: aggregate over (SELECT DISTINCT player_id, salary, ... FROM contracts). A team's payroll counts every row on that team.
5. [lineup_keys] Join lineup_stats, lineup_bootstrap on lineup_uid only (it contains the season and team). lineup_bootstrap lacks 32 lineups, so use LEFT JOIN from lineup_stats.
6. [find_player_in_lineup] lineup_stats.lineup is player ids joined by '-'. To test membership use ('-' || lineup || '-') LIKE ('%-' || <player_id> || '-%'). A bare LIKE '%<id>%' also matches longer ids. lineup_stats.players holds FAMILY NAMES only, comma-separated.
7. [names_and_ids] Resolve a person to player_id first, then filter by id. players has first_name and family_name (with diacritics, e.g. Jokić, Šarić). Full name = first_name || ' ' || family_name. Teams: team columns named `team` and *_abbr hold 3-letter abbreviations (BOS); *_team_id columns hold ids; join teams to translate.
8. [units] Ratings are points per 100 possessions. poss is a real number because possessions are split half-and-half between the two sides. Percentages in *_pct columns are fractions 0-1. Salaries are whole US dollars.
9. [players_traded] A player's team is a fact about a game, not the player (players has no team_id). Use player_game_stats.team_id for who a player played for. player_season.teams is text like 'WAS → DAL' for a traded player.
10. [games_results] games has home and away points, no winner column and no ties. Home win = home_pts > away_pts. Each team plays 82 games. game_date is ISO text (YYYY-MM-DD).
11. [always_bound_results] Add LIMIT to any query that lists rows, and prefer aggregating in SQL.

METRICS
- off_rating: pts_for / poss_for * 100: points scored per 100 possessions.
- def_rating: pts_against / poss_against * 100: points allowed per 100 possessions (lower is better).
- net_rating: off_rating - def_rating, per 100 possessions. Observed, noisy, garbage time excluded.
- poss: Possessions the lineup played, (poss_for + poss_against) / 2. The sample size.
- shrunk: Empirical-Bayes estimate of the lineup's true net rating: the observed rating pulled toward the league mean (-0.68) in proportion to how little was observed. Use this to rank lineups.
- post_sd: Posterior standard deviation of shrunk. lo95/hi95 = shrunk -/+ 1.96 * post_sd.
- weight: Share of the observed rating that survives shrinkage, 0-1; rises with possessions.
- distinguishable: 1 if the 95% interval excludes the league-average lineup rating, i.e. lo95 > mu or hi95 < mu where mu = noise_model.mu (-0.68); else 0. Two of the four flagged lineups have lo95 slightly below 0, so this is NOT the same as "excludes zero".
- net_rating_luck: net_rating after resetting OPPONENT three-point and free-throw conversion to league rates (36.1% and 78.4%); attempts are unchanged. A luck-adjusted view of the same lineup.
- rapm: Regularised adjusted plus-minus: a player's estimated impact in points per 100 possessions after adjusting for teammates and opponents. o_rapm + d_rapm = rapm. Pooled across all loaded seasons (here only 2025-26). Noisy below a few thousand possessions; check poss.
- ppp: Points per possession in a play type. For defence this is points ALLOWED per possession, so lower is better.

TABLES (use describe_table(name) for columns and sample rows)
- teams [one row per team]: The 30 teams.
- players [one row per player (591)]: Player directory.
- games [one row per game]: Final scores of the 1,230 regular-season games.
- player_game_stats [one row per player per game (32,179)]: Box score line per player per game, including players who did not play.
- player_season [one row per player (577)]: Season totals of on-court possessions and net margin per player.
- player_rapm [one row per player (582)]: Player impact estimate (RAPM) from the lineup ridge model.
- lineup_stats [one row per lineup per team (17,733)]: Every five-man lineup of a team with its rating and uncertainty.
- lineup_bootstrap [one row per resampleable lineup (17,701; 32 lineups missing)]: Cluster-bootstrap check of lineup intervals (a robustness cross-check on lineup_stats).
- noise_model [single row]: Parameters of the empirical-Bayes model behind shrunk (one row).
- coverage_season [single row]: Season-level data quality of the play-by-play reconstruction (one row).
- coverage_team [one row per team (30)]: Data quality per team.
- contracts [one row per player per team (414 rows, 408 players)]: 2026-27 player contracts.
- cap_rules [one row per season]: Salary cap thresholds for 2025-26 and 2026-27 (two rows).
- player_positions [one row per player (582)]: Listed position per player.
- play_types [one row per play type]: Lookup of the 11 play types.
- player_play_type_stats [one row per player per play type per side (5,937; minimum 10 possessions)]: Player efficiency by play type, offence and defence.
- team_play_type_stats [one row per team per play type per side (660)]: Team efficiency by play type, offence and defence.
- provenance [one row per table]: Where each table in this database was copied from. Not useful for basketball questions.

The best five-man lineup in the league by noise-corrected net rating (`shrunk`) is the Charlotte Hornets lineup consisting of Miles Bridges, LaMelo Ball, Moussa Diabaté, Brandon Miller, and Kon Knueppel (player IDs: 1628970-1630163-1631217-1641706-1642851). 

Over 998.5 possessions, this lineup achieved an observed net rating of +27.26 points per 100 possessions, and an empirical-Bayes shrunk net rating of +17.27 (with a 95% interval of +8.12 to +26.41), making it statistically distinguishable from the league-average lineup. 

In total, out of 17,733 five-man lineups in the database, only 4 are statistically distinguishable from league average (where the 95% confidence interval excludes the league-average lineup rating of -0.68). Raw net ratings without shrinkage are heavily distorted by small sample sizes (for instance, over 53.5 possessions, a San Antonio Spurs lineup had a raw net rating of +104.9).
caveats: Rankings use shrunk (empirical-Bayes noise-corrected net rating) per rule #1 to account for small sample sizes.
